key_insight: The paper introduces frame width as a new design parameter for quantum codes, showing that low-weight logical bases can exist only when code structure and symmetry constraints are carefully matched.
engineering_relevance: For fault-tolerant quantum computing, these results help estimate qubit and compilation overheads more accurately by pairing code distance with the actual weight of a complete logical basis.
method: Define frame width f as the smallest weight cutoff that still allows a full canonical logical basis.
Analyze structural obstructions and sufficient conditions for group-valued CSS codes, including odd-order vs. power-of-two group behavior.
Demonstrate the framework on high-rate lifted-product and pair-partition codes, plus a symmetry-reduction distance-certification workflow.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports explicit examples including an [[1088,128,22]] lifted-product code with f=22 and an [[1024,256,24]] pair-partition code with f≤27, alongside exact distance certification for codes with more than a thousand qubits.
watch_item: Frame width is not always equal to distance, so designers should not assume minimum-weight logical operators form a complete canonical basis.
paper_title: Designing Group-Valued Codes with Full Regular Low-Weight Bases
